angle: The format's most famous 'combo tribe' turns out to be its fairest famous deck — zero combo lines in the 99, a floor-3 bracket resting on two tutors alone — while the entire step-up waits on a 21-card bench, where the checker refuted the celebrated Dinosaur two-card 'infinite' as a whole-table draw-machine and verified the correct alternative, a line you only maximize by declining a trigger.

THE SAFE POLYRAPTOR: seven tokens, and perfect play means saying NO to a trigger
ONE-SIDED APOCALYPSE: your Dinosaurs take 1 each while 16 damage hits a player
10,000 GOLDFISH GAMES: the honest number is eight — and 54.6% never cast him at all

violators.text: ZERO COMBOS IN THE 99 — WE CHECKED

departments.note: Full-bleed Gishath, Sun's Avatar art_crop (Zack Stella, LCI 229 — credit per §9). Masthead, Vol. 7, August 2026, $4.95 from issue.json verbatim. Authored tagline 'Seven damage, then the ground shakes.' sits under the logotype. The dominant coverline names stack 002's verdict because the refutation is this issue's most exciting verified thing (§7.6): the database's famous Dinosaur infinite is, in this deck as built, a mandatory loop that draws the whole table. Every tease maps to a delivered spread — no inflation.

Two buckets: THIS ISSUE'S DECK (First Turns through Judge's Desk highlights with their promises, not just titles) / EVERY ISSUE (standing departments). Reprint the full three-tier legend — ✓ checker-passed, ◆ seeded artifact, ★ labeled coaching. Flag the Kill spread and the four case files A-001–A-004 as the issue's spine. One line of honest framing: 'This issue's maindeck contains zero combo lines. That is not a typo; it is the story.'

departments.headline: BATTLECRUISER IN NAME ONLY
departments.dek: Everyone at the table thinks they know this deck: big lizards, big turns, fair fun. So why does the pilot's manual tell you to plan your attack like a combo turn? Because under the scales this is a linear critical-mass deck — seven quiet turns of deflection compressed into one protected pivot.
departments.body: Open on the question the reader already has: what is an 8-mana commander deck DOING for seven turns? Answer in three moves, drawing on manual_prose.how_it_wins. One: the win is a single trigger — Gishath connects, reveals cards equal to damage dealt, and free-rolls every Dinosaur among them; 34 bodies in 65 nonland spells make the reveal dense, and Case A-001 prices one clean hit at five bodies, three draws, and a discover at X=6. Two: the honest cost is the number eight — mean cast turn 7.932 in the goldfish, 9% by turn 6 — and the deck attacks it from two sides, ramp (82% of games see ramp or fixing by turn 6) and the cheat/reducer layer (56% by turn 6: Urza's Incubator, Otepec Huntmaster, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Descendants' Path). Three: the payoff arrives as one wrath-sized package — the trigger IS the wave — so the swing is timed like a combo turn: protection held, table's mana counted, sweeper assumed. Close on the thesis: there is no combo behind the curtain (zero contained lines, floor 3 on two tutors), and that fairness is a feature you will spend the whole issue learning to weaponize.

captions.Gishath, Sun's Avatar: **THE WHOLE DECK IN ONE TEXT BOX:** combat damage to a player reveals that many cards and free-rolls every Dinosaur among them — vigilance, trample, and haste mean the swing happens the turn he lands.
captions.Pantlaza, Sun-Favored: **THE SECOND ENGINE:** once per turn, an entering Dinosaur discovers X equal to its toughness — no combat, no eight mana, and it keeps working the turn after a wrath.
captions.Urza's Incubator: **THE REAL ACCELERANT:** Dinosaurs cost {2} less, turning your commander into a six-drop. The goldfish's 7.93 mean cast explicitly ignores this card — it is why your games run faster.

pilot_tips.text: Never plan to activate Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual with Unclaimed Territory's mana — it casts creature spells only, so it accelerates the cast plan and never the cheat plan.

departments.pull_quote: The trigger is the wave. You cannot deploy in waves — so you learn to time the tide.

departments.headline: THE EIGHT-MANA GUARANTEE
departments.dek: What is guaranteed access worth when the card costs eight? Everything — this deck mulligans without ever looking for its win condition, because the win condition lives in the command zone. The catch is that the guarantee runs one way: the zone always offers Gishath, but the tax makes sure you can only really afford him once.
departments.body: Four teaching blocks. ZONE (✓, cite CR 903 command-zone access): the deck runs zero backup wincon density because the payoff is always castable from the zone — that is why Keep or Ship never asks 'do you have a threat?'. THE TAX LADDER (✓, CR 903.8): first cast {8}, second {10}, third {12} — set against the goldfish's mean available mana of 6.476 on turn 8 and 7.331 on turn 10, the deck never organically reaches a second cast in the simulated window. Conclusion, coached (★, strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance): protection is arithmetic, not caution — each uncovered removal spell costs the {2} tax plus a tempo turn, roughly two full turns, and two answered casts effectively ends your game. Flawless Maneuver costs zero with your commander out; it is THE swing-turn card. COLOR IDENTITY (✓, CR 903.4): Naya buys the best creatures and protection suite in the format and permanently locks out counterspells — your only interaction with a stack is Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard ping. THE CLOCK (✓, CR 903.10a): 7 power means exactly three connections for 21 commander damage — and because the reveal scales with damage dealt, the commander-damage plan and the value plan are the same swing; Boros Charm's double strike makes it two hits and a 14-card reveal. THE POLITICAL READ (★): Gishath is public information from turn zero; every sweeper at the table is being held for your pivot, not the token player's board.

captions.Gishath, Sun's Avatar: **THE COMMANDER FILE:** {5}{R}{G}{W}, Naya identity, goldfish mean cast 7.932 (median 8). Tax ladder: 8 → 10 → 12. The zone guarantees the card; the ladder is why you protect it instead of recasting it.
captions.Boros Charm: **THE CLOCK COMPRESSOR:** double strike turns a three-connection commander-damage kill into two — and doubles the reveal to 14 cards on the way.

pilot_tips.text: Hold Flawless Maneuver through your own attack, not just theirs — it costs zero while you control your commander, and the wrath you should be assuming comes after the trigger banks.

departments.pull_quote: The zone always offers him back. The ladder makes sure you can only afford him once.

departments.headline: THE HONEST NUMBER IS EIGHT
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded goldfish games, and the headline finding is the one the deck least wants printed: mean commander cast turn 7.932, median 8, and 5,460 of 10,000 games never cast him by turn 10. Here is why that number is the ceiling of the problem — and what the deck does about it.

callouts.title: THE COMMANDER CURVE
callouts.text: Cast-turn distribution: 9% by turn 6, the mode at turn 8 (1,360 games), and 54.6% of games never casting him by turn 10. The stated-assumptions box governs the read: the simulator does not model cost reducers or cheat-into-play effects, so 7.932 is the ceiling of the problem, not your expectation.

callouts.title: WHAT THE DECK DOES ABOUT IT
callouts.text: Ramp or fixing drawn: 90.2% of games overall, 82% by turn 6, mean turn 2.232. Cost reducer or cheat piece drawn: 67.2% overall, 55.9% by turn 6, mean turn 3.004. The two-front attack on the number eight, measured.

callouts.title: THE MID-GAME SAG
callouts.text: Land-drop hit rate falls from 99.9% on turn 1 to 51.9% by turn 6, and mean available mana at turn 6 is just 5.494 — the deck ramps early, then leans on rocks and dorks. Exactly the profile a mid-game sweeper punishes twice: board AND mana.

callouts.title: THE SWING-TURN KIT
callouts.text: Connection kit (haste or evasion for the big attacker) by turn 6: 51.2%. Protection held for the board by turn 6: 49.2%. Enrage engine drawn by turn 6: 48.7%. Three coin-flips the pivot turn wants to win — the politics pages teach you to hide which ones you lost.

captions.Sol Ring: **MEASURED, NOT VIBES:** the opening-hand policy (keep 2–5 lands) kept 77.2% of first sevens with a mean of 0.279 mulligans — your floor, not your standard. Keep or Ship raises the bar.

pilot_tips.text: Read every power meter on this page knowing the simulator ignores this card — the 56% cheat-layer figure is drawn-by-turn-6, and any one of those pieces beats the 7.93 mean by turns.

departments.pull_quote: The simulation is only a simulation — and it says so in print, every issue.
departments.note: ◆ costume throughout; every figure verbatim from goldfish_metrics.json. The stated-assumptions box is non-negotiable and should sit adjacent to callout 1, not below the fold.

departments.headline: SEVEN DAMAGE, THEN THE GROUND SHAKES
departments.dek: One unblocked hit and the checker counted the receipts: five bodies, three cards, a discover at X=6 — and the whole cascade turns on putting nine triggers on the stack in the right order. Then the same verification loop walked onto the bench, refuted the most famous Dinosaur 'combo' in the game, and found the line that actually works.

callouts.title: THE CONNECTION
callouts.text: Gishath attacks the open seat unblocked and deals 7. The trigger resolves: reveal seven — Regisaur Alpha, Ripjaw Raptor, Carnage Tyrant, and Ravenous Sailback are Dinosaur creature cards and hit the battlefield; Cultivate, Mountain, and Path to Exile bottom in a random order. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-001 →

callouts.title: ONE EVENT, NINE TRIGGERS
callouts.text: All four enter simultaneously as a single event. Regisaur Alpha's haste covers the newcomers, Garruk's Uprising sees three of them at power 4+, and Pantlaza, Sun-Favored offers its once-per-turn discover. Nine triggers, one controller — you — and you choose the order of every one.

callouts.title: THE ORDERING LESSON
callouts.text: Put Carnage Tyrant's Pantlaza trigger on top so the once-per-turn discover resolves first at X=6, and put Regisaur Alpha's token trigger on the bottom: the 3/3 arrives after the discover is spent, misses Garruk's Uprising at power 3, and re-triggers nothing. Stack it token-first and you are dared into a discover at X=3 instead.

callouts.title: THE RECEIPT
callouts.text: Net from one 7-damage connection: five new bodies, three cards drawn, a discover at X=6 — all hasty, all one combat too late without an extra-combat effect. This is why the manual says one connection replaces an entire turn cycle of casting.

callouts.title: REFUTED: THE DRAW-MACHINE
callouts.text: The database flags Marauding Raptor + Polyraptor as infinite tokens. The checker's verdict: every trigger in the loop is mandatory, the 2-damage ping never kills a fresh 5/5, and this deck as built holds no exit — so the loop ends when an opponent breaks it on their terms, or the rules draw the game for the whole table. Both cards are benched, and now you know why they must never share the 99. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-002 →

callouts.title: VERIFIED: THE SAFE LOOP
callouts.text: Forerunner of the Empire + Polyraptor is the same engine with a hand on the throttle — the ping is 'you may', once per Dinosaur entry, with a safe stop at every link. Verified maximum: 7 tokens, and reaching it requires DECLINING one intermediate trigger; saying yes to everything caps you at 6. The chain self-terminates when Forerunner dies to its own third sweep. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-003 →

callouts.title: VERIFIED: THE ONE-SIDED ACT
callouts.text: Blasphemous Act deals 13 to each creature; Temple Altisaur caps your OTHER Dinosaurs at 1 each; benched Wrathful Raptors throws every point your team is dealt at a non-Dinosaur target. The accounting: Temple Altisaur eats its own 13 and dies — but still redirects 13 via last known information — and 16 total damage lands on one player while the opposing boards are already swept. From 26 life: down to 10, devastating but not lethal alone. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-004 →

captions.Carnage Tyrant: **THE PRIORITY TRIGGER:** hexproof, uncounterable, and the biggest toughness in the reveal — its Pantlaza trigger is the one you resolve first, for a discover at X=6.
captions.Regisaur Alpha: **HASTE FOR THE HERD, TOKEN LAST:** its static gives the free-rolled army haste immediately; its 3/3 token trigger goes to the bottom of the stack so it arrives after the discover is spent.
captions.Polyraptor: **ONE ENGINE, TWO VERDICTS:** with Forerunner of the Empire it is a verified 7-token burst; with Marauding Raptor it is a verified whole-table draw. The difference is two words in oracle text: 'you may.'

pilot_tips.text: Stack the biggest toughness's Pantlaza trigger to resolve first — the discover is once per turn, so spend it at X=6, never at X=3.
Decline one intermediate Forerunner ping so a second enrage token is on the battlefield before the final sweep — mashing yes caps you at 6 tokens instead of 7.

departments.pull_quote: THE DATABASE SAID INFINITE. THE RULES SAID: EVERYBODY LOSES.
departments.note: Peak spread of the issue. Callouts 1–4 are the maindeck kill (Case A-001); callouts 5–7 are the bench's verified physics and must carry a visible 'BENCH' tag on their card images — these lines are not in the 99 today, and the spread says so plainly. Rules numbers stay in Judge's Desk; the narrative here carries the teaching.

departments.headline: THE MOST TELEGRAPHED DECK IN THE ROOM
departments.dek: Gishath sits in the command zone as public information from turn zero, and every opponent who has ever seen the card knows the plan is one combat trigger. So how do you keep a table from wrathing a deck whose entire game is one announced swing? You manage what they can price in — and hide what they cannot.

callouts.title: THE QUIET-RAMP DISCOUNT
callouts.text: Your turns 1–4 posture — Cultivate into Skyshroud Claim — buys peace with new tables and nothing with experienced ones: anyone tracking mana knows what Naya ramp under an 8-drop commander means. Assume the posture is discounted, and bank its value early.

callouts.title: SEQUENCE THE TELL
callouts.text: Urza's Incubator or Belbe's Portal on turn 3 moves the table's read of your clock up by two full turns and invites the pre-emptive strike. Deploy cheat pieces as late as the line allows, and never end-of-turn Worldly Tutor the turn before your cast unless you are committed.

callouts.title: UNCERTAINTY IS ARMOR
callouts.text: You hold board protection in only 49% of games by turn 6 — and that gap is precisely why you never reveal whether you have it. A table that KNEW you were coverless would wrath on sight; a table that suspects Flawless Maneuver waits, and waiting is what your curve needs.

callouts.title: THE THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: The moment the trigger banks — five bodies, three draws, a discover at X=6, per Case A-001 — you are the archenemy no matter how you posture. From that board, plan to end the game within one table rotation: Regisaur Alpha haste plus Overwhelming Stampede math, or a second connection. The table will not give you two.

captions.Rogue's Passage: **THE BLOCKER MATH:** a 4-toughness chump eats lethal assignment and shaves your reveal from 7 to 3 even through trample. Passage's {4} buys a guaranteed 7-card reveal and zero blocker interaction — it beats the pump whenever a real blocker exists.
captions.Worldly Tutor: **THE LOUDEST INSTANT IN THE DECK:** an end-step tutor the turn before eight mana tells three opponents exactly when the ground shakes. Cast it committed or not at all.

pilot_tips.text: Spend pump mana only into genuinely open lanes — the reveal scales with damage DEALT, so a pumped swing into a chump block converts to nothing while Rogue's Passage converts to seven cards.

departments.pull_quote: You have protection 49% of the time. The table doesn't know which 49% — keep it that way.

departments.headline: NINE MANA, TWO BLUE SEATS
departments.dek: Two boards from real Gishath turns. In the first, your commander is resolving with one mana open and a lane that exists this turn only. In the second, nine triggers are about to hit the stack and only one order is right. Commit to your line before you turn the page — the recommendations wait below the branches.

callouts.title: PUZZLE ONE: SWING OR HOLD?
callouts.text: Turn 8, precombat main. Gishath was cast for eight — first cast, no tax — and is on the stack with one mana still open; Rogue's Passage is NOT affordable this turn. Seat A is Azorius flash control with two blue up. One seat cannot block profitably. Do you swing now on one free trick, or untap into the covered line? Three branches, then our answer.

callouts.title: PUZZLE TWO: ORDER THE CASCADE
callouts.text: Combat damage step: Gishath connected for 7, and the reveal put Regisaur Alpha, Ripjaw Raptor, Carnage Tyrant, and Ravenous Sailback onto the battlefield under Pantlaza, Sun-Favored and Garruk's Uprising. Nine triggers, one once-per-turn discover, and you choose every position. Which trigger goes on top — and which goes to the bottom?

captions.Flawless Maneuver: **THE FREE INSURANCE:** the card that changes puzzle one's math — with your commander on the battlefield it costs {0}, which means holding open mana is not the same thing as holding an answer.

departments.pull_quote: Assume every held answer appears the moment the 8-drop hits the stack — then count what you can pay for.
departments.note: Renders from decisions/001-swing-or-hold-gishath.json and decisions/002-pantlaza-discover-order.json. Hard rule: recommendation strictly after the branches, and neither headline nor board copy may telegraph 'swing' as correct in puzzle one. Puzzle two deliberately echoes the Kill's ordering lesson — reading the spread first is not cheating, it's the curriculum.

departments.headline: WHO HOLDS THE WRATH FOR YOU
departments.dek: Every archetype at the table prices your deck the same way: one big turn, then a reckoning. Four threat files on who actually collects — and the named outs, all of them already sleeved in your 99.

callouts.title: SWEEPER CONTROL — THREAT: SEVERE
callouts.text: Your worst frame: the Gishath trigger builds a one-wrath board, and deploy-in-waves is structurally unavailable. Outs: Flawless Maneuver and Boros Charm beat destroy-based sweepers; Heroic Intervention adds hexproof against the targeted follow-up; Akroma's Will covers both with the commander out; Eerie Interlude is the only out to -X/-X, sacrifice, and exile wraths — but it abandons your tokens, so it is the desperation line. Time the pivot into their tapped-out turn; rebuild through Pantlaza, Sun-Favored plus the draw engines.

callouts.title: FAST COMBO — THREAT: SEVERE
callouts.text: The bad seat: zero maindeck combos, no counterspells in Naya, and a clock that starts near the 7.93 mean. Outs: Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, and Beast Within go at enablers on sight; Trumpeting Carnosaur's discard mode is instant-speed reach at a creature enabler; Belbe's Portal deploys Gishath at instant speed the end step before your combat. Held answers rot — spend now.

callouts.title: STAX — THREAT: HIGH
callouts.text: Taxes hit an 8-drop harder than anyone at the table, so the fight is over your cheat layer, not your payoffs: mulligan toward the 56% (Urza's Incubator, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Descendants' Path), keep dorks deployed against land-tax pieces, and aim Thrashing Brontodon, Beast Within, and Austere Command at the specific piece that turns the cheat layer off — not the scariest permanent.

callouts.title: DEATHTOUCH TABLES — THREAT: MODERATE
callouts.text: Your enrage math inverts against deathtouch: Temple Altisaur's prevention leaves 1 through, and 1 deathtouch damage still destroys. Stop offering Ripjaw Raptor into those blocks; bring your own damage instead — Blasphemous Act under Temple Altisaur deals your team exactly 1 each (Case A-004) — and Rogue's Passage dodges the block entirely.

captions.Eerie Interlude: **THE DESPERATION OUT:** the only answer to exile and -X/-X wraths — but it abandons your tokens and returns the bodies at end step. Whether Pantlaza's discover fires off the return still needs a stack scenario, so don't count on the rebate.

pilot_tips.text: Against combo, spend Trumpeting Carnosaur from your hand as the discard ping at their enabler — the 7/6 body is a luxury the bad seat cannot afford.

departments.pull_quote: Every sweeper at the table is being held for YOUR pivot turn — plan like you can see it.

departments.headline: SIXTY-FIVE SPELLS, ONE JOB
departments.dek: Why does a deck about one trigger need ninety-nine cards? Because every slot either accelerates toward the trigger, cheapens it, protects it, rigs it, or cashes it in — and once you can name a card's job, you know exactly when to spend it.
departments.body: Card-tile grid grouped by job, ranked within group, prose from manual_prose.card_roles. Groups, in reading order: THE PAYOFF CORE (Gishath, Sun's Avatar; Pantlaza, Sun-Favored; Descendants' Path; Etali, Primal Storm; Carnage Tyrant; the 34-body herd — lead with the load-bearing five, tile the rest); THE ACCELERANT LAYER (21 lands + Cultivate/Kodama's Reach/Nature's Lore/Skyshroud Claim, five rocks, four dorks, and the cheat/reducer tier: Urza's Incubator, Otepec Huntmaster, Belbe's Portal, Monster Manual // Zoological Study, Mirari's Wake); THE PROTECTION SUITE (Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm, Akroma's Will, Eerie Interlude); INTERACTION (Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Beast Within, Triumphant Chomp, Bronzebeak Foragers, Thrashing Brontodon, Blasphemous Act, Austere Command, Wakening Sun's Avatar); THE RIGGING (Congregation at Dawn, Worldly Tutor, Enlightened Tutor — the two Game Changers that alone set the bracket floor at 3); THE CONNECTION KIT (Rogue's Passage, Kessig Wolf Run, Hunter's Insight, Overwhelming Stampede). Then the separate labeled strip: THE BENCH — 21 cards, zero of them in the 99, holding the entire step-up package; pointer to Upgrade Watch.

captions.Descendants' Path: **THE REPEATABLE CHEAT:** every upkeep, a revealed Dinosaur gets cast free — and with 34 bodies the hit rate is real. Casting, not putting, matters for cast triggers.
captions.Wakening Sun's Avatar: **READ THE FINE PRINT:** it wipes non-Dinosaurs only if you CAST it from your hand — a Gishath free-roll or Portal activation gets the body and skips the wrath. Sequence accordingly.
captions.Zacama, Primal Calamity: **THE CAST-ONLY REFUND:** its lands-untap clause triggers on casting from your hand, so a free-roll delivers the removal engine but not the mana rebate.
captions.Secluded Courtyard: **READ THE CLAUSE, NOT THE PHRASE:** its mana casts Dinosaur spells AND activates abilities of Dinosaur sources — so it pays Zacama, but never Belbe's Portal or Monster Manual.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Congregation at Dawn before a Gishath connection, not after — three creatures stacked on top turns the reveal from a lottery into a delivery.

departments.pull_quote: Roughly 40% of the deck makes or reduces mana. That is not padding — that is the price of the number eight.
departments.note: Ranked, not encyclopedic (anti-pattern: completionism). Six cards have no role tag (Descendants' Path, Eerie Interlude, Hunter's Insight, Overwhelming Stampede, Rishkar's Expertise, Triumphant Chomp) — the taxonomy lacks patterns, not the cards functions; the grid places them by their real jobs and says so in a footnote.

departments.headline: SEVENTY-FOUR HANDS, ONE HERD
departments.dek: Nobody painted this deck — seventy-four people did. Across 107 card entries there is no standout hand, and that breadth is the story: a tribe assembled across eight years of sets, with the biggest single contribution just six cards wide.
departments.body: Breadth feature, per the analysis: standout is null and the lead cluster is six cards, so no curation story gets invented. Hero image: the commander — Gishath, Sun's Avatar by Zack Stella (LCI 229), credited per §9. Lead cluster: Simon Dominic, 6 entries, every one a Dinosaur or Dinosaur spell (Curious Altisaur, Kinjalli's Sunwing, Triumphant Chomp maindeck; Apex Altisaur, Ranging Raptors, Silverclad Ferocidons on the bench — the gallery labels the bench cards honestly). Second: Tyler Jacobson, 5 entries — with the honest footnote that two of them are the same card, the deck's maindeck-plus-spare pair of Wakening Sun's Avatar, so his distinct-card count is four. Also worth noting strip: Daarken painted both maindeck halves of the Case A-004 line (Blasphemous Act and Temple Altisaur) plus Otepec Huntmaster; Sam Burley painted both Pantlaza, Sun-Favored and Secluded Courtyard; Mark Tedin's pair (Belbe's Portal, City of Brass) spans a quarter-century of the game. Art File facts: 107 entries, 121 copies, 74 artists, 0 accessories, 0 foils, 0 borderless; frame effects run to 10 legendary crowns. Counting note printed verbatim in spirit: per-entry is the honest basis — Forest is one entry despite 8 copies, or the count would inflate Maojin Lee.

captions.Curious Altisaur: **THE LEAD HAND:** Simon Dominic's six Dinosaurs make him this deck's widest contributor — six cards of one tribe, half of them still waiting on the bench.
captions.Temple Altisaur: **ONE PAINTER, ONE COMBO:** Daarken painted both maindeck pieces of the verified one-sided sweep — the shield and the thirteen damage it redirects.

departments.pull_quote: The biggest hand in a 107-card collection painted exactly six of them.
departments.note: No drop_runs, no roster overlap flagged — there is no bought-whole product story to tell and none is invented. Counts are recomputed by the renderer from artist-credits; the plan supplies only the framing and prose.

departments.headline: MULLIGAN FOR THE ENGINE, NOT THE PAYOFF
departments.dek: The goldfish's loose policy — keep any seven with two to five lands — kept 77.2% of hands. That is your floor, not your standard: your commander is guaranteed, so every mulligan question is really an acceleration question. Four hands; make your call before reading the verdicts.

callouts.title: HAND ONE
callouts.text: Forest, Plains, Command Tower, Sol Ring, Cultivate, Urza's Incubator, Carnage Tyrant. VERDICT: KEEP — easily. Ramp on curve plus the deck's scarcest resource: a cheat/reducer piece is drawn by turn 6 in only 55.9% of games, and this hand already holds the headline one.

callouts.title: HAND TWO
callouts.text: Ghalta, Primal Hunger; Zetalpa, Primal Dawn; Zacama, Primal Calamity; Etali, Primal Storm; two Forests, Mountain. VERDICT: SHIP. All payoff, no engine — mean available mana at turn 6 is 5.494 and the land-drop hit rate has already sagged to 51.9% by then. The deck does not organically climb to eight; hands like this ask it to.

callouts.title: HAND THREE
callouts.text: Unclaimed Territory, Jetmir's Garden, Alpine Meadow, Belbe's Portal, Drover of the Mighty, Regisaur Alpha, Boros Charm. VERDICT: SHIP — and know why. Every land enters tapped or restricted; nothing deploys the turn-two rock line on time, and Unclaimed Territory can never activate the Portal this hand is banking on.

callouts.title: HAND FOUR
callouts.text: Forest, Mountain, Drover of the Mighty, Otepec Huntmaster, Kodama's Reach, Garruk's Uprising, Ripjaw Raptor. VERDICT: KEEP, eyes open. Dork-heavy keeps are real acceleration that dies to the sweepers this deck most fears — Kodama's Reach is the land-based ramp piece that makes this keep responsible rather than fragile.

captions.Cultivate: **THE STANDARD-BEARER:** 82% of games see ramp or fixing by turn 6, mean turn 2.232 — a keepable hand almost always has it, so a hand without it is below your deck's own average.

pilot_tips.text: Keep one land-based ramp piece alongside any dork-heavy hand — dorks are acceleration that dies to the wrath you are supposed to be assuming.

departments.pull_quote: Your win condition is in the command zone. Your mulligan is about everything else.
departments.note: ★ verdicts grounded in ◆ figures — cite 77.2% keep rate, 0.279 mean mulligans, and the target rates exactly. Hands are authored drills, deterministic, drawn from manual_prose.mulligan's ship/keep classes.

departments.headline: BENCH PRESS
departments.dek: This deck's upgrade path doesn't run through a shopping list — it runs through its own 21-card bench, where the entire combo and enrage package sits out the maindeck's floor-3, zero-combo posture. Eight ranked swaps under the pilot's aggressive mandate, every delta 3 → 3, and one pair that must never be sleeved together.

callouts.title: THE MANA TIER
callouts.text: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds in for Ravenous Sailback (the promote case: turn-2 Selvala plus any 4-power Dinosaur puts Gishath castable around turn 5–6 against a 7.93 mean, and 34 bodies feed her draw); Regal Behemoth in for Verdant Sun's Avatar (monarch draw plus land-doubling on a 5/5 that defends its own crown).

callouts.title: THE VERIFIED ENRAGE PACKAGE
callouts.text: Forerunner of the Empire in for Goring Ceratops — it rigs the Gishath reveal, converts ETBs into Ripjaw Raptor draws under Temple Altisaur's cap, and is the safe half of Case A-003. Polyraptor in for Zetalpa, Primal Dawn — ONLY alongside Forerunner, and only while Marauding Raptor stays benched. Wrathful Raptors in for Earthshaker Dreadmaw — completes Case A-004 with two cards already maindeck.

callouts.title: THE MUTUAL EXCLUSION
callouts.text: Swap 8 — Marauding Raptor in for Otepec Huntmaster as a strictly wider reducer — exists ONLY for the build where Polyraptor stays benched. Case A-002's verdict is absolute: together they are a mandatory loop that draws the whole game, breakable only by an opponent's choice, and this deck runs no sacrifice outlet to break it itself. One or the other. Never both.

callouts.title: THE HONEST LEDGER
callouts.text: The bench holds no Game Changers, so all eight swaps are power WITHIN bracket 3, not a bracket move — but promoting the Polyraptor package changes what the deck IS at a table, not just how fast it wins. Make the swap deliberately, and say so when you sit down. The obsolescence index, for its part, offers almost nothing tuned to typal fit — its one actionable note is the strict ramp family (Three Visits, Farseek beside the Nature's Lore class already here), and we say so out loud.

captions.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: **HIGHEST ROI ON THE BENCH:** a 3-mana engine aimed at the deck's defining problem — with the one political rider that her draw clause is symmetric, so hold her when an opponent's deck lands the table's biggest bodies.
captions.Ranging Raptors: **RAMP THAT SURVIVES THE WRATH:** every ping fetches a basic — mana on lands instead of on dorks that die to the deck's own Blasphemous Act.

pilot_tips.text: Never sleeve Marauding Raptor and Polyraptor in the same 99 — the loop is mandatory, this deck holds no exit, and the verified outcome is a draw for the whole table.

departments.pull_quote: Two of the three headline packages are not what they look like — which is exactly why we checked.

departments.headline: PROVE IT
departments.dek: Four cases this issue: the cascade that pays five bodies for seven damage, the famous 'infinite' that draws the whole table, the safe loop that rewards saying no, and the thirteen points that came back off a dead shield. Every citation verbatim, every verdict stamped.

callouts.title: CASE A-001 — THE TRIGGER CASCADE
callouts.text: Gishath connects for 7: what one reveal actually unleashes, and why trigger order decides whether the discover lands at X=6 or X=3. VERDICT: PASS, 2 iterations.

callouts.title: CASE A-002 — THE DRAW-MACHINE
callouts.text: Marauding Raptor + Polyraptor: infinite tokens, or a mandatory loop with no exit? VERDICT: PASS, 2 iterations — the loop draws the game for the whole table unless an opponent chooses to break it.

callouts.title: CASE A-003 — THE CONTROLLABLE BURST
callouts.text: Forerunner of the Empire + Polyraptor: maximum 7 tokens, safe stop at every link, self-terminating — and the maximum requires declining a trigger. VERDICT: PASS, 1 iteration.

callouts.title: CASE A-004 — THE ONE-SIDED ACT
callouts.text: Wrathful Raptors + Blasphemous Act + Temple Altisaur: your Dinosaurs dealt 1 each, the shield takes its own 13 and still redirects it via last known information, 16 total to one player. VERDICT: PASS, 2 iterations.
